why: The student gives a correct general definition of an infinite loop (its condition stays true, so it never stops) but does not apply it to this code, where i += 0.5 is truncated back to 0 and i never changes.

concepts.quote: A loop that never stops because its condition stays true.
concepts.why: It correctly names the behaviour and its cause in general terms but does not trace i or the int cast in this code.
It indirectly states the correct rule that a loop keeps repeating while its condition is true, without applying it to i < 10.
Nothing is said about the init, the update or the loop variable.
There is no convergence test in the code or the answer.
